subject: Mid-contract top-up: staggered bundling conversion + SLA carveouts
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine@brightway.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightway.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring mid-contract top-up + co-term options

Diego —

Quick note from Brightway as we evaluate a mid-year usage bump. We're projecting roughly a 60–80% uplift in generation volume starting Aug 1 (steady-state over next 6 months). A few asks:

- Can we add capacity mid-contract and amortize to our existing annual term (co-term)?
- Are there structured bundle options that let us stagger increases (e.g., month 1: +30%, month 3: additional +30%) with predictable unit pricing?
- We need a temporary SLA carveout for burst capacity during expected peaks — can Redwood guarantee latency SLOs or provide credits for misses?

If possible, please send a short proposal we can share with procurement/legal. Budget holder is cc'd (procurement@brightway.ai). We prefer a solution that minimizes invoicing churn — monthly billing okay if it ties back to our annual commitment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call next week if that helps.

Best,
Elaine Wu
Head of Platform
Brightway AI

Attachment: none

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine@brightway.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring mid-contract top-up + co-term options

Elaine —

Appreciate the detail. I've sketched three pragmatic paths that balance predictability and operational overhead; attaching a one-page proposal for quick review. High-level:

Option A — Immediate top-up (simple, higher unit price)
- Fast add-on; billed monthly.
- No co-term; higher uplift rate to reflect ad-hoc capacity.

Option B — Staggered bundle conversion (recommended)
- We convert your incremental usage into a staged bundle tied to the existing annual term.
- Example: Aug 1 add +30% (Tier 1 rate), Nov 1 add additional +30% (Tier 2 rate, slightly discounted).
- Billing: monthly line items that roll up to the annual commitment (keeps invoicing aligned).

Option C — Annualize early (higher credit, one-off amendment)
- Move a portion of future spend into the current agreement; triggers a midterm amendment and pro-rata invoice.

SLA carveouts and burst capacity: we can support a temporary higher SLO for latency with an agreed carveout fee or a credit schedule for misses. For brightway-sized bursts, we typically include a 15% burst buffer on top of dedicated capacity; anything beyond gets auto-routed to overflow pools (slower but cheaper).

Next steps I recommend:
1) If Option B looks good, confirm the target %s and preferred ramp dates.
2) I'll loop in Finance/Legal to prepare the amendment + a redline MSA if procurement needs it.
3) We can put a DocuSign packet together once terms are agreed.

I've cc'd Kimberly (pricing ops) — she'll send a pricing matrix and a nominal discount table — and Marissa (your AE) for customer success coordination. Proposal attached.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: staged-bundle-proposal.pdf (PDF, 175KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mid-contract top-up + co-term options — pricing inputs

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks — quick pricing clarifications from ops/finance:

- If Brightway wants staged bundling (Option B), recommend we anchor Tier 1 at +30% at a 8% uplift discount vs Option A; Tier 2 (additional +30%) at 12% uplift discount. Rationale: protects base economics while giving a meaningful incentive to consolidate.
- For SLA carveout: propose a temporary 0.5% of monthly ARR fee for the enhanced latency SLO, with a credit ladder that scales to 25% of that fee if SLO misses exceed thresholds.
- Legal redline: procurement typically requests a service credit cap and a limited liability carveout for burst routing. We should draft a one-paragraph SLA amendment and a short MSA addendum.

I've attached the pricing matrix and a draft redline. Marissa — can you confirm if CS is okay with the proposed ramp dates and the 15% burst buffer? If Brightway wants a larger buffer we should price accordingly.

-Kim

Attachment: pricing-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB); redline-msa.docx (DOCX, 32KB)

From: Elaine Wu <elaine@brightway.ai>

Diego / Kim / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Brightway elects Option B (staggered bundle conversion) with the following confirms:

- Ramp: Aug 1 +30%; Nov 1 additional +30%.
- We accept the proposed discount splits (8% then 12%).
- SLA carveout: we'll accept the temporary fee model but would like the credit ladder to be explicit in the amendment. Procurement attached our PO for the initial Aug addition; please confirm whether you want a separate invoice or a single consolidated invoice tied to the annual term.

Two small asks before DocuSign:
1) Can you add an explicit statement that overflow routing will not be used for PII-sensitive traffic (we'll mark those requests and keep them on dedicated lanes)?
2) Please include an explicit SLO credit table for misses >50ms and >200ms.

If you can send the MSA addendum + DocuSign packet I can get procurement to sign ASAP.

Best,
